interactions.summary: Aurelia says Paradiso sounds far more transcendent and beautiful than Inferno, and Jiang answers that Dante is likely trying to mirror the universe's vibrations through lighter heavenly sounds and heavier infernal ones.

Aurelia offers a staccato Inferno example, and Jiang says Dante intentionally controls syllables and hard versus soft consonants, adding that without real Italian knowledge the Comedy is almost impossible to understand.

One student speculates that Italian's Latin endings make rhyme and flow easier, another asks about the rhyme or cadence scheme, Aurelia notes that English rhymed translations are poor, and Jiang redirects the discussion toward meter and asks for the stress pattern to be explained on the board.

claims.claim: Aurelia says Paradiso feels much more transcendent and beautiful to read aloud than Inferno.
Jiang guesses Dante is trying to mirror the vibration of the universe, using lighter sounds for heaven and heavier or harder sounds for the lower realms.
Jiang says Dante can produce these different effects by intentionally controlling syllables and the balance of hard and soft consonants.
Jiang says that unless one truly understands Italian, it is almost impossible to understand the Divine Comedy.
A student proposes that Italian's Latin-style endings make rhyme easier and give the language a smoother flow than English.
Aurelia says English rhymed translations exist but are generally poor compared with the sonic force of the Italian.
Jiang shifts the class from rhyme to meter and asks for the stress pattern to be formally explained.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang imagines Dante tuning sound to cosmology, with the poem's phonetics mirroring the universe's vibrational structure.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Dante is trying to mirror the vibration of the universe
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the key leap from literary technique to metaphysical architecture in the packet.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang raises the bar brutally: without real Italian, readers will miss the Comedy at its deepest level.
signature_moments.source_phrase: unless you truly understand Italian, it's almost impossible to understand the Divine Comedy
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This gives the public read Jiang's most uncompromising statement about linguistic access.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The stress pattern Jiang wants the class to map explicitly as a way of understanding Dante's formal power.

uncertainty_notes.note: The ASR likely compresses Jiang's contrast between heavenly and infernal sound textures; the stable point is that he maps different phonetic qualities onto different cosmic levels.
